result:
With `view_order_reversed` on, the web UI now puts live flows at the front of the list. I haven't run the tests or the type-check.

**Cause.** The web app never read `view_order_reversed`. The initial `/flows` fetch was already reversed, because the server iterates its view in reversed order. Live `flows/add` and `flows/update` events were sorted client-side with a comparer that treats all flows as equal, so new flows always landed at the end.

**Change**, in `web/src/js/ducks/flows/index.ts`:
- `FlowsState` has a new `reversed` field, kept in sync from the `OPTIONS_RECEIVE` and `OPTIONS_UPDATE` actions. When it changes, the view is rebuilt in the new order.
- `makeSort` takes an optional arrival-index map. When given, ties are broken newest-first. The add, update, receive, remove, filter-update and set-sort paths all pass it when `reversed` is set, so a column sort also shows newer flows first among equal values.
- When no sort column is set, clearing the sort restores list order, reversed if the option is on.

**Tests.** I added `reversed: false` to the test state in `__tests__/ducks/tutils.ts`. I also added a spec in `__tests__/ducks/flows/indexSpec.tsx` that turns the option on, adds flows a, b and c, and expects the view order c, b, a. The spec passes a partial options payload with `as any`.
